# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment
The verified baseline uses 6 LUTs and 4 FFs, passes simulation, and has routed setup slack of 0.528 ns and hold slack of 0.009 ns. The core registers `index` and `valid` on `clk`, clears both synchronously when `rst` is high, and otherwise selects the highest asserted request bit while setting `valid` from whether any request bit is set. Numeric latency is unknown, so preserve the exact observable cycle behavior. With only 6 LUTs, improvement may be limited; promotion requires strictly fewer LUTs and all existing gates to pass.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the nested priority chain with shared request-group prefix reductions and direct equations for the three index bits may reduce duplicated priority logic and lower LUT use while preserving the same registers and cycle behavior.

## Instruction for generator
In `priority_encoder8_core`, replace the `if`/`else if` priority chain that assigns `index_reg` with shared combinational reductions for request groups `[7:4]` and `[7:6]`, then derive each index bit from the highest-priority asserted request. Keep `valid_reg <= (request != 8'd0)`, the synchronous active-high reset assignments, and the existing clocked registers unchanged. For an all-zero request, continue assigning index zero; preserve priority for every multi-bit request.
